purpose: Local source-of-truth ledger for city-culture R&D. It preserves research from collaborative sessions before any optional database promotion or embedding work.
recent_change: Added the North Platte ordinary-evening evidence pass (owner Packet 2): all four rhythm-calibration evidence-bar items satisfied, the event-led assignment corrected, and the calibration row graduated to complete. Also completed verification of the Elko marketing-pole pack (verbatim Reddit excerpts, Dotty's address).

storage_policy.neon_policy: No ledger entry is imported to Neon by default.
storage_policy.embedding_policy: Only entries marked embedding_ready may be chunked and embedded; raw numbers are retained as structured evidence, not treated as embeddings.

status_definitions.conversation_captured: Preserved from this research conversation; may lack complete source URLs or independent verification.
status_definitions.source_linked: A source URL is recorded, but scope, vintage, or interpretation still needs review.
status_definitions.locally_normalized: Claim, source, scope, counterevidence, and limitations are represented in a checked-in local artifact.
status_definitions.embedding_ready: A bounded evidence passage has source URL, retrieval date, city scope, stance, and no unresolved attribution gap.
status_definitions.promotion_review: Candidate for an explicitly approved R&D database import; never implies production approval.

entries.claim: Elko is a small mining-centered regional city with visible Western, Basque, and outdoor civic institutions.
limitations: Does not establish a representative after-hours pattern.
Does not establish newcomer integration or school/hunting behavior.

entries.claim: On an ordinary Tuesday, Elko is not dead after 8 p.m. but its after-dark menu is narrow: several bars stay open late (Charlee's karaoke to 2 a.m., the Underground to midnight, Rubies to 11), while dinner service closes by roughly 8:00-9:30. The scene is bar-, casino-, and karaoke-centered rather than a broad nightlife district.
entries.source_gap: Resolved for the six named venues (hours verified and re-confirmed 2026-08-07). Charlee's, Mattie's, and Rubies are primary (own sites); Star and Underground are corroborated-aggregator (3-4 agreeing listings, no first-party hours page). One residual gap: the 'Garage Bar' lead could not be tied to a real Elko venue and is dropped pending identification.
limitations: One weekday pattern cannot establish citywide or weekend nightlife.
Venue marketing and an open door do not prove actual crowd intensity; a representative weekday foot-traffic sample is still missing.

entries.claim: The reviewed local corpus cannot support a conclusion about whether Elko is a good place to raise a trans teenager; adjacent claims about general politics, specialist care, and social integration are not valid substitutes for school climate, youth support, or trans-specific care evidence.
limitations: This abstention describes the reviewed corpus, not Elko itself.
No new external evidence was collected because the purpose is to test an evidence-bound refusal.

entries.claim: Odessa shares industrial-work and constrained broad-nightlife signals with Elko, but is a larger Permian Basin oilfield regional-city subtype rather than an Elko equivalent.
limitations: Midessa accounts can mix Midland and Odessa.
A first four-venue Tuesday-hours pass now exists in data/gold-packs/odessa-vs-elko-after-dark.claims.json; a fuller Odessa-only venue inventory is still missing.

entries.claim: On an ordinary Tuesday, Odessa and Elko share the same after-dark rhythm - dining winds down ~9:30, then a narrow, car-dependent bar-and-karaoke scene, each with a nightly-karaoke bar open to 2 a.m. - but Odessa (~6x larger) sustains several 2 a.m. bars where Elko sustains about one. The difference is depth by population, not nightlife type; oilfield-vs-mining barely shows after dark.
limitations: Evidence is asymmetric by design: the Elko side is a re-confirmed six-venue pack, the Odessa side a same-day four-venue pass, and Odessa lived-texture rests on r/Midessa (Midland+Odessa blur).
'Several vs one' 2 a.m. bars is a directional depth difference from small samples, not a full late-venue census.

entries.claim: North Platte has continuous industrial activity centered on Bailey Yard but a socially event-led or venue-led evening pattern; industrial wakefulness must not be mistaken for broad nightlife.
limitations: Superseded in part on 2026-08-19: the ordinary-week venue-hours sample now exists (north_platte_ordinary_evening_2026), and it corrected the event-led assignment — the ordinary venue layer is real; events amplify rather than constitute the evening.

entries.claim: Lincoln County voted 12,674 Trump/Vance to 3,586 Harris/Walz in the certified 2024 presidential result, supporting a strongly conservative county-level proxy.
entries.scope: Lincoln County, not North Platte city-only
limitations: A city-specific descriptor requires aggregating the North Platte precincts; county totals include rural voters.

entries.claim: Conversation research treats family compatibility as moderately supported but corrects both hyper-rootedness and boomtown transience: the available residence-mobility evidence suggests a middle position pending full benchmark capture.
limitations: Demographics and mobility do not directly prove family norms, newcomer welcome, or multigenerational rootedness.

entries.claim: Elko, Odessa, and North Platte may belong to a broad blue-collar regional-hub family, but each is a distinct subtype: mining/outdoors, oilfield/industrial, and railroad/agriculture/service respectively.
limitations: This is a research hypothesis, not a similarity score or recommendation.

entries.claim: Irvine consistently ranks among the safest large cities in the U.S., with a violent crime rate around 84 per 100,000 (versus the national average of ~359), yielding a TCI of 23. Crime is not a material quality-of-life concern relative to most large Southern California cities.
limitations: FBI-based reporting lag; 2024 data is the latest available.
Crime rate is citywide; neighborhood variation is not captured.

entries.claim: Irvine's median home sale price is approximately $1.52 million, with cheaper pockets around $967k (ZIP 92606). At current mortgage rates (~6.7%), plausible homeownership requires roughly $250,000 household income at minimum, and a typical family home ($1.2M–1.6M) requires $350,000–400,000. A 20% down payment on the median is about $305,000 before closing costs.
limitations: Redfin median is a point-in-time snapshot; market conditions fluctuate.
Income thresholds assume 20% down, ~6.7% rate, and ~1.1% property tax with HOA — actual requirements vary by loan product and buyer situation.
Irvine has significant condo/townhome inventory that is cheaper than detached homes; the $250k income floor is for condo-level entry, not detached-family-home entry.

entries.claim: Bowling Green's standardized 2024 violent-crime rate supports the stored low violent-crime index, while property crime and theft are the practical safety concern; reported rape is a notable offense-mix outlier and 2025 BGPD figures are useful local context but not a replacement for finalized FBI UCR.
limitations: OpenCrime and PlainCrime are secondary mirrors of FBI UCR/CDE data; the direct FBI API was not used for the one-city row.
BGPD 2025 year-end operational figures are not finalized FBI UCR and should not overwrite the 2024 UCR-based TCI.
Citywide rates hide neighborhood-level variation.

entries.claim: Bowling Green has an in-city VA outpatient clinic for routine care, mental health, labs, telehealth, social work, and nutrition; full VA medical-center care remains regional, with Nashville stored as the nearest VA medical center, and VA announced a larger outpatient clinic lease in August 2026.
limitations: The larger clinic is planned/future access, not current capacity.
The row's 1-mile outpatient distance is centroid-to-facility distance, not proof the clinic is outside city limits.
VA hospital access remains separate from outpatient clinic access.

entries.claim: Elko's official marketing (Explore Elko, Elko Area Chamber, Travel Nevada) and resident accounts describe the same after-dark inventory - bars, casinos, live music, karaoke, two 24-hour gaming-bar listings - but marketing frames it as generalized evening energy while residents describe the same list as basically the whole menu; the divergence is category breadth, not factual disagreement.
limitations: Marketing quotes were re-verified verbatim against live pages on 2026-08-19, and all six cited Reddit threads are verified (two pre-existing corpus sources; four captured verbatim by the owner the same day).

The 24-hour operation of Bourbon Street Sports Bar and Dotty's was corroborated 2026-08-19 by the Elko Junction landlord tenant pages (no venue-primary hours page exists for either); Casino City corroborates Dotty's 1744 Mountain City Hwy address, with a store-number rendering inconsistency (#35 vs #53) outstanding.
Event evidence (Sippin' Saturday, Ghost Tours) is labeled event evidence, not ordinary-night nightlife.

entries.claim: North Platte's ordinary weeknight has a real venue layer - taverns to 1 a.m., dining/brewery/lounge/recreation to about 10 p.m., an independent coffee shop out by 3 p.m., and one genuine 24/7 diner - so 'event-led, not venue-led' fails in its strong form; social breadth contracts sharply by category as the night advances while Bailey Yard runs a documented 11 p.m.-7 a.m. shift clock, and organized events (weekly Wednesday dances, seasonal concerts, festivals) periodically widen the evening well beyond the regular layer.
limitations: Ten venues across six categories is representative by design but partial; Hub Bar's hours are recorded as unknown (not closed), so late tavern depth may be understated.
Availability only: no attendance or foot-traffic measurement.
Brothers Tavern hours are directory-sourced and Merrick's hours are Chamber-sourced with a first-party breakfast-hours conflict on opening time; both marked lower confidence.
The lived accounts are 13 years apart (2010 City-Data vs 2023 Niche) and neither is weeknight/weekend specific.
